dirty_claims.detail:
**This chore covers only {{n}} nodes (the ones listed below) — done when those are fixed.** This is not a request to clean up the whole store — there are still {{total}} dated nodes in the store, and **those don't need attention right now** — read on for why.

**Why it's worth a few minutes**: the claim line is the **only thing exposed** in search results. A dirty body only misleads you when you expand it; a dirty claim **misleads you on every single search**. The new gate added in this version only covers what you write from now on — what's already in the store won't fix itself.

**This batch** (picked because these are the ones you use most — fixing them has the highest payoff):
{{sample}}

**The only criterion: does this sentence guide action right now?**
- Yes → keep it, even if it's about an incident from three months ago
- It's just recording "something happened on a certain day" → that's a chronicle — delete and rewrite

Dates are part of the claim when **they belong** ("banto name deprecated after 8-11"); delete them when they're just a timestamp on a conclusion ("8-16 done: append replaced by section+write" → should read "section-level write uses section to read hash + write to replace the whole section, optimistic lock prevents accidental overwrites").

**How to fix (zero risk)**:
```
memory_upsert(id="<slug>", claim="claim: ...")
```
🔴 **Pass only claim, never body** — fields you don't pass are not touched, the body is left completely intact. All edits to the original are fully logged in history; `memory_admin(op='revisions')` can recover them — you can always undo.

---

**What to do with the rest — two legs, neither requires scheduling:**

1. **Fix on touch.** Next time you `memory_touch` a dirty one, the receipt will flag it on the spot — that's the moment when all the context you need is right at hand, the cheapest time to fix it.
2. **No touch? Small batches over time.** `memory_admin(op='doctor')` surfaces 5 items at a time, ranked by heat. Cold nodes with bad claims **don't affect any search** — let them be bad.

🔴 **Don't try to fix the whole store at once.** It's not feasible, and it shouldn't be done — an undoable checklist trains this track into noise, and then even the items that should be done get skipped.

Aside: your store also has {{provisional}} claims that were machine-generated from old summaries during migration and **have never been verified by a human** — they look identical in search results to claims you personally validated. Same fix, same two legs, no dedicated schedule needed.
